author: root Codex personal critical interface design
name: IOMMU后有界物理前缀历史与正常AXI响应
basis: Concrete weaker-integration alternative, based on actual TC normal translated AR/response path and ordinary physically tagged read-history cache semantics; not an assertion a retrieved paper already implements the exact endpoint.
contract: Same trusted stable immutable Normal source/order scope; independently successful own READ permission before requester data response; same separately charged history capacity as the honest quarantine shim; same cache/AR/prot/user compatibility and original per-ID obligations.
algorithm: Observe actual issuer downstream physical source AR accepted and its true R handshakes. Save a bounded contiguous prefix with physical tag/attrs/provenance; stop capturing when full, without holding issuer READY for a late requester.

Requester follows its normal original untranslated READ and native TL/TC path. When the requester normal physical AR appears, keep it immutable and accept it as a local physical cache endpoint after actual authorization assurance; this is a real AR handshake, not cancellation.

Lookup matching physical tag, source-snapshot validity, range and compatible attributes. If p prefix words match, emit them in order as ordinary requester R with the original AR ID. They enter iDMA FIFO/progress only after requester own READ is confirmed.

Emit at most one downstream requester suffixAR covering the remaining N-p words, in the same source page/envelope, and reconstruct its responses under the original accepted AR. Only final original offset has RLAST.

Miss uses one ordinary full downstream requester AR. Denied permission produces no history response and invokes the proper native error route/real failed-job path; missing access_ok/FPD distinctions cannot be wished away.

Keep source tags and response/miss records through all held VALID and real handshakes; preserve per-ID original request order and true downstream miss R obligations. Every original WRITE and B remains untouched.
cost: Bounded history payload/tag/valid mask/provenance; never count that capacity as a free existing iDMA FIFO.
Accepted original physical AR response descriptor and offset cursor, hit-prefix/replay and one suffix descriptor; optional multiple outstanding support needs paid per-ID queue/MSHR.
Lookup/response arbitration and extra datapath cuts; tag must remain valid for whole replay or preserve accepted-hit payload snapshot.
Live join during an issuer burst requires response ownership/capacity; simpler prefix replay after issuer completion does not assume it.
Authorization assurance plus native real job errors still required for candidate and control; unchanged error-only flags are not sufficient proof.
Immutable-source/coherence/lease administration charged equally; no generic coherence claim.
counts: For a retained hit prefix p: issuerN plus requester suffixN-p = 2N-p payload R, at most2 downstream dataAR; full match N/AR1; miss2N/AR2. Upstream requester physicalAR is accepted to local cache and completed normally; it is not counted as an extra DDR read.
comparative_capability: This obtains the same serial-cold prefix savings and zero requester data exposure before own permission with normal post-translation physical request processing. It avoids raw-load/adopt of iDMA FIFO, original-READ cancellation, and separate nonclaiming prepare origin for this bounded case.
limits: No executed implementation; actual cache-hit/miss service cost unmeasured. A mismatched actual grant naturally chooses a different physical-tag lookup; general remap/revocation remains outside stable contract. A speculative pre-grant scheme may still have a different useful latency/storage point, but it must demonstrate it rather than use the common retained-prefix count.
novelty_gate: Because a completely specified post-IOMMU history endpoint realizes the retained-prefix bound under a simpler original-response contract, the bound alone cannot justify the extra pre-grant adoption interfaces. This is an architectural comparison, not firstness denial from an imagined copy of the whole new scheme.
